pr_title: kernel: mem_domain: let k_mem_domain_*() functions to return errors
pr_body:
This changes the `k_mem_domain_*()` functions to return errors. See individual commits for more details.

Fixes #24609
pr_comments: Buildkite failure due to tests taking too long to run. No individual test failure reported.

issue_context.title: Propagate error values and remove assertions in kernel/mem_domain.c
issue_context.body:
**Problem description**
For now k_mem_domain APIs need an overhaul, none of them propagate return values and there is not enough checking done. A lot of HW specific requirements on partition base addresses, sizes, and the number of partitions. This isn't being completely checked at runtime.
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/kernel/mem_domain.c 

**Possible solution**
Add return values to APIs and add additional checking according to the architecture used.

review_comments: I saw, most of the `CHECKIF` replaces the origin `__ASSERT`, but this one does not. I am curious why keeping `__ASSERT ` here.

Would it make it more readable to reverse the polarity of this?  There are several places like this in the PR.  I see that you just changed the __ASSERT to CHECKIF and added the !, but I think it might be more readable as
CHECKIF(sys_dyn_regions_num >= len)

I thought about that, but decided not to. It is to keep the core of the conditionals the same as in `__ASSERT()`. So that the brain doesn't have to parse twice, as long as one understands that `__ASSERT() => !CHECKIF()`.
